title: Presentation
description:
Open-source JSON format for describing PowerPoint presentations. Agents describe narratives, content, audience, reusable assets, and design — the engine handles OOXML complexity.

Content references (Slide.layout, design.theme, design.colorScheme / design.colorScheme.id, design.fontScheme / design.fontScheme.id, narrative, audience, purpose and tone, and the colorScheme / fontScheme a theme record names) point at catalog records. Each is a bare 'id' or a 'name:id' whose prefix names a group in 'catalogs'. A bare id resolves in catalogs.custom, then in the records embedded under catalogs.default, then in the catalog the host registered for catalogs.default.source (or the host's default catalog when 'default' is omitted); 'name:id' resolves in catalogs.<name>, then in the catalog the host registered for its source. A reference that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference, and the slide uses automatic composition or the engine default. Engines never fetch a catalog: a saved document embeds every record it uses, and hosts register any other catalog by its source string. See docs/default-catalog.md.

chart.type, the language tag and the keys of Organization.socials / Speaker.socials are engine vocabularies, validated directly with no catalog lookup. When a document names no theme, colour scheme or font scheme, every engine uses the same small engine defaults (spec/reference/engine-defaults.json). Asset references use 'asset:<id>' strings that point into the top-level assets registry, and content color fields (rich-text runs, styled table cells) accept hex values, color-scheme slot/role names, or 'var:<id>' references into the top-level variables map.

$schema.description: Optional OPF schema version. When omitted, validators and engines should assume the latest supported OPF schema.

name.description: Display name of the presentation for GUI/TUI lists, library/search indexing, OS-level metadata, and default export filenames. This is deck identity, not slide content. Use slides[].title and slides[].subtitle for text that should appear on presented slides. Also the built-in variable 'deck.name'.

description.description: Free-form prose describing what this presentation is about. Used by agents and humans as a deck-level summary; complements purpose (the goal) and narrative (the structured storyline). Round-trips to OOXML 'docProps/core.xml' as '<dc:description>' (PowerPoint surfaces this as the 'Comments' field in File → Properties). Also the built-in variable 'deck.description'.
examples: Quarterly business review covering revenue, product, and hiring milestones for the executive team.

filename.description: Optional base filename for exports (without extension). The opf CLI (render, export) and the editor strip a trailing .pptx, .pdf, .png, or .svg (case-insensitive) and append the target format's extension. When omitted, they slugify name; with no usable name the CLI uses the input file name and the editor uses 'presentation'. See /docs/opf for full validation rules.

organization.description: Organization associated with the presentation, usually the presenting company. Array form supports hosts, partners, clients, and sponsors. The primary organization (Organization.role 'primary', else the first item) supplies the cover and section logo, the 'socials' header/footer field and the 'organization.<field>' built-in variables; the others are available by id as 'organization.<id>.<field>' and are not drawn automatically.

speaker.description: Person presenting the deck. Array form supports panels and multi-speaker decks. The first speaker is the primary speaker: the built-in variables 'speaker.<field>' read it, 'speakers' lists every name, and 'speaker.<id>.<field>' addresses one by id. A speaker is drawn nowhere else.

author.description: Optional credit for the person who authored or contributed to the deck, distinct from speaker. Array form supports multiple contributors. Round-trips to OOXML 'docProps/core.xml' as '<dc:creator>' (semicolon-joined when multiple) and seeds '<cp:lastModifiedBy>' on first write; subsequent edits in PowerPoint overwrite '<cp:lastModifiedBy>' with the editing user. Also the built-in variable 'deck.author' (an array joined with ', ').

audience.description:
Intended audiences for the presentation. Accepts any of:
- A single string: an audiences reference ('executive', or 'acme:board' for a record of the catalogs.acme group), or free-form text ('Series B investors'). A string that is a bare id or 'name:id' is a reference; any other string is free text and is never looked up.
- A single inline Audience object, for custom audience metadata or overrides on a referenced record. Object form has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-audience/v1.
- An array of strings and/or inline Audience objects, for more than one audience.

A reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference. Nothing is drawn from the audience.

purpose.description:
Primary goal of the presentation. Accepts either:
- A string: a purposes reference ('decide', or 'acme:fundraise' for a record of the catalogs.acme group), or a free-form goal ('Raise a Series B round of $30M'). A string that is a bare id or 'name:id' is a reference; any other string is free text and is never looked up.
- An inline Purpose object for custom purpose metadata or overrides on a referenced record. Object form has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-purpose/v1.

A reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference. Nothing is drawn from the purpose.
examples: Raise a Series B round of $30M

language.description:
Language of the presentation content, an engine vocabulary: a BCP-47 language tag, validated directly with no catalog lookup. Accepts either:
- A BCP-47 tag ('en-US', 'en-GB', 'ja', 'zh-Hans', 'ar-SA').
- An inline Language object: a 'bcp47' tag plus overrides of what engines know about it (name, ooxmlLang, script, direction, the script font schemes).

Engines know the script, base direction, OOXML language tag and default script fonts of the tags in spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json; any other well-formed tag is accepted and its script is inferred from the tag. Language names and descriptions are catalog display metadata, not part of the document.

tone.description:
Desired tone for the presentation. Accepts either:
- A tones reference: a bare id ('formal') or 'name:id' for a record of a named catalogs group.
- An inline Tone object for custom tone metadata or overrides on a referenced record. Object form has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-tone/v1.

A reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference. Nothing is drawn from the tone.

takeaway.description: Audience-facing takeaway the presentation should leave behind. Array form supports multiple takeaways. Deck-level intent used by AI to seed and pressure-test slide content.
examples: Agent latency is the new bottleneck for AI products.
Agent latency is the new bottleneck for AI products.
Our runtime is 8x faster than the next-best option.
Customers see ROI within the first quarter.

duration.description: Target presentation duration, as an integer number of minutes. The opf-render presenter view counts the elapsed time against it, and core validate warns when it lies outside the resolved narrative's 'duration' range. Agents can also use it to set pace and depth. Nothing else reads it: the preview and the PPTX export draw no duration.

tags.description: Free-form labels used for categorization, search, and filtering. Lowercase kebab-case is recommended for consistency across a deck library.

design.description: Optional design system covering theme, color scheme, font scheme, dimensions, background, logo, watermark, header, and footer applied to the deck. When omitted, engines use their default design configuration.

variables.description: Optional named variables: deck colors referenced as 'var:<id>' (the original use), and typed content variables (text, number, date, image, url, list) referenced inline as '{{<id>}}' or whole as 'var:<id>'. Variables are what makes a deck a fillable template when combined with 'template': true. Color variables complement the color scheme: scheme slots and roles stay the primary vocabulary; variables cover deck-specific named colors that have no scheme slot. Built-in variables ('{{speaker.name}}', 'var:organization.logo', 'deck.name', ...) need no declaration; see Variables.

template.description: Marks this document as a template: an incomplete OPF file. A template declares variables (top-level 'variables') and references them from content, and may leave required variables unfilled; validation then reports the unfilled variables instead of failing, and previews and exports use each variable's 'example'. Filling a template (resolveVariables, or 'opf fill') returns a normal deck with this marker removed. Absent or false: a normal deck, where an unfilled required variable is an error. See docs/templates-and-variables.md.

narrative.description:
The deck's narrative plan, by reference: a bare narratives id ('classic-story') or 'name:id' for a record of a named catalogs group ('acme:founder-pitch'). The deck holds only this pointer; the plan (the arc, its beats and what each beat must do) lives in the record, which has the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-narrative/v1. A narrative the document defines itself is a record in catalogs.custom.narratives, referenced here by its key.

Slides link themselves to beats with slides[].beat. Core validate warns about a slides[].beat id the resolved narrative does not define and about a root 'duration' outside its 'duration' range, and reports a beat that no slide references. The preview and the PPTX export draw nothing from the narrative; opf-pptx stores the reference for round-trip.

The reference resolves like every content reference (see catalogs); one that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference, never an error.

Deck-level concerns that are not part of the storyline (audience, tone, takeaway, duration) live as siblings on the presentation root.

slides.description: Ordered array of slides that make up the presentation.

references.description: Sources that text runs cite with 'cite'. Ids are unique. A cited reference is listed in the footnote area of every slide that cites it, with a marker number assigned per deck in order of first use; a reference no run cites is the warning opf/unused-reference. referencesSlide() turns the cited references into an ordinary list slide.

examples.text: Gartner, Market Guide for Presentation Tooling, 2026

datasets.description: Optional shared data tables, keyed by id. A chart ('chart.data': { "dataset": "<id>" }) or a table ('table': { "dataset": "<id>" }) references one instead of holding its own copy; engines inline the reference before composing, rendering or exporting. A dataset nothing references is the warning opf/unused-dataset. See docs/chart-table-data.md.

assets.description: Optional reusable asset registry for images, data files, videos, documents, fonts, and other resources referenced elsewhere in the deck via 'asset:<id>' strings.

catalogs.description: The catalog records this document embeds, grouped by the catalog they came from: 'default' (the catalog bare ids come from), 'custom' (records the document defines itself) and any number of named catalogs ('acme', referenced as 'acme:<id>'). A saved document embeds every record it references, so it renders the same with no catalog registered. See Catalogs.

extensions.description: Custom data passthrough for agent workflows; ignored by the engine but preserved across read/write round-trips.

Assets.description: Reusable asset registry for resources used by slides, charts, metadata, and design. Keys are stable asset ids referenced elsewhere as 'asset:<id>'. Each asset can be a source string or an object with src plus optional metadata.

Asset.description: Reusable or inline resource. A string is shorthand for { "src": value }. Source strings accept 'asset:<id>' references, HTTPS URLs, data URIs, relative paths resolved against the OPF file location, or local filesystem paths. Use object form when metadata such as alt text, title or mediaType matters.

src.description: Resource source. Accepts an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, relative path resolved against the OPF file location, or local filesystem path.

alt.description: Alternative text for images and other visual assets.

title.description: Human-readable asset title for editors and asset pickers.

description.description: Optional notes about the asset's contents, provenance, or intended use.

mediaType.description: Optional MIME media type when it cannot be inferred from src.

Audience.description: Inline audience metadata for the presentation. Use 'id' to reference an audiences record (a bare id or 'name:id') and override selected fields, or use 'name' for a custom inline audience.

id.description: Optional audiences reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved before applying the inline overrides.

name.description: Human-readable audience name shown in pickers.

description.description: Longer prose describing the audience and how to address them.

seniority.description: Typical seniority level of the audience.

technicalFluency.description: Typical technical fluency of the audience.

decisionPower.description: Whether the audience is expected to be informed, advise, or decide.

attentionBudgetMinutes.description: Realistic upper bound on focused attention for a single presentation, in minutes.

recommendedNarratives.description: Soft cross-link: narrative ids that work well for this audience, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

recommendedTones.description: Soft cross-link: tone ids that work well for this audience, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

tags.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

Purpose.description: Inline purpose metadata for the presentation. Use 'id' to reference a purposes record (a bare id or 'name:id') and override selected fields, or use 'name' for a custom inline purpose.

id.description: Optional purposes reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved before applying the inline overrides.

name.description: Human-readable purpose name shown in pickers.

description.description: Longer prose describing when to use this purpose and how it should shape a deck.

outcome.description: Desired audience outcome after the presentation.

successCriteria.description: Observable signals that the deck accomplished this purpose.

recommendedNarratives.description: Soft cross-link: narrative ids that work well for this purpose, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

recommendedTones.description: Soft cross-link: tone ids that work well for this purpose, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

tags.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

Language.description: Inline language metadata for the presentation: a BCP-47 'bcp47' tag plus overrides of what engines know about it. Languages are an engine vocabulary, not catalog records, so there is no 'id'.

bcp47.description: BCP-47 language tag used for locale-aware rendering, proofing, and accessibility metadata. Use 'en-GB' for UK English; 'en-UK' is not a valid BCP-47 region form.

ooxmlLang.description: Culture tag for OOXML text-run language attributes (a:rPr/@lang, a:endParaRPr/@lang), in the language-[Script-]REGION form Office recognizes (e.g. 'ja-JP', 'ar-SA', 'ms-MY', 'nb-NO', 'fil-PH', 'zh-CN'). Without it, engines emit the curated tag of their language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) for a tag without a region, and a region-bearing tag as written. Curated rather than inferred so output does not depend on the runtime's locale data.

code.description: ISO 639-3 or 639-2 language code carried for engines that prefer ISO codes.

direction.description: Base text direction for the language. When omitted, engines derive it from the script: Arabic (Arab), Hebrew (Hebr), Syriac (Syrc), Thaana (Thaa), N'Ko (Nkoo), Adlam (Adlm), Samaritan (Samr), Mandaic (Mand) and Hanifi Rohingya (Rohg) are right-to-left; every other script is left-to-right. The engine language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) states it for the tags it knows.

script.description: ISO 15924 script code of the language's writing system. The script selects the OOXML font slot the language's text uses: East Asian scripts (Hans, Hant, Hani, Jpan, Kore, Hang, Hira, Kana, Bopo, Yiii) use the eastAsian slot; complex scripts (for example Arab, Hebr, Syrc, Thaa, Deva, Beng, Guru, Gujr, Orya, Taml, Telu, Knda, Mlym, Sinh, Thai, Laoo, Tibt, Mymr, Khmr, Mong) use the complexScript slot; every other script (Latn, Cyrl, Grek, Armn, Geor, Ethi, ...) uses the latin slot. When omitted, engines infer it from the BCP-47 tag. The engine language vocabulary (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json) states it for the tags it knows. See docs/programs/font-fidelity-everywhere/script-font-model.md.

fontScheme.description: Font-scheme reference (a bare id or 'name:id') for this language's script slot when targeting PowerPoint output. Its major/minor families fill the language's script slot (eastAsian or complexScript, chosen by 'script') unless the effective design font scheme sets that slot itself; the latin slot always follows the design font scheme. Without it, engines use the default script fonts of their language vocabulary.

googleFontScheme.description: Font-scheme reference (a bare id or 'name:id') used in place of 'fontScheme' when resolving script fonts for Google Slides output.

summary.description: One-sentence note about coverage or font defaults.

description.description: Longer prose describing the language record and any font-pairing rationale.

tags.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

Tone.description: Inline tone metadata for the presentation. Use 'id' to reference a tones record (a bare id or 'name:id') and override selected fields, or use 'name' for a custom inline tone.

id.description: Optional tones reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved before applying the inline overrides.

name.description: Human-readable tone name shown in pickers.

description.description: Longer prose describing the tone and the kinds of decks it suits.

voiceCues.description: Short directives that shape AI generation toward this tone.

avoid.description: Anti-patterns that AI generation should not produce when this tone is active.

samplePhrases.description: Short example phrases that exemplify this tone.

recommendedNarratives.description: Soft cross-link: narrative ids this tone pairs well with, for picker UIs. Never resolved, embedded or validated as references.

tags.description: Free-form labels for filtering and search.

Organization.description: An organization associated with the presentation, typically the presenting company, but also hosts, partners, clients, or sponsors. The primary organization (role 'primary', else the first one) supplies the cover and section logo (unless design.logo overrides it) and the 'socials' header/footer field (its socials). Every field is also a built-in variable ('{{organization.name}}', 'organization.<id>.<field>'), and every logo a slide-scoped image ('var:organization.logo.icon', 'var:organization.<id>.logo'). Nothing else about an organization is drawn automatically. See docs/templates-and-variables.md.

id.description: Stable identifier for the organization, used to reference it from Speaker.organizationId and to address it in built-in variables as 'organization.<id>.<field>'. Must be unique among organizations (a duplicate is a validation error).

name.description: Display name. The built-in variable 'organization.name' (primary organization) or 'organization.<id>.name' carries it into any string, such as a header or footer text of '{{organization.name}}'.

legalName.description: Optional legal entity name when it differs from the display name. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'organization.legalName'.

logo.description: The organization's logo. A path, URL or Asset is one logo for every shape; an object gives up to four shapes (full, stacked, icon, wordmark), each a path or Asset, or { onLight, onDark } for the two backgrounds. A path is resolved against the OPF file location; an HTTPS URL, data URI or 'asset:<id>' reference works too. SVG (preferred for vector logos) or PNG with transparency are typical. The primary organization's full logo (role 'primary', else the first organization) is drawn on cover and section slides unless design.logo names another or is false. Every logo is also a slide-scoped built-in image, placed with a whole-field reference in any image field: 'var:organization.logo' (the full logo), 'var:organization.logo.icon' (likewise stacked, wordmark, full), and 'var:organization.<id>.logo' or 'var:organization.<id>.logo.<shape>' for another organization. A missing shape falls back to full, and full to the first defined of wordmark, stacked and icon. The onLight or onDark value is chosen for each slide's background; a missing one uses the other. See docs/templates-and-variables.md and docs/design-resolution.md.

domain.description: Bare internet domain for the organization. Never drawn automatically and not used to look up assets; available as the built-in variable 'organization.domain'.

email.description: General contact email for the organization. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'organization.email'.

phone.description: Main contact phone number for the organization. E.164 format is recommended. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'organization.phone'.

tagline.description: Short tagline. Never drawn automatically (cover slides do not show it); available as the built-in variable 'organization.tagline', for example in a footer 'text' of '{{organization.tagline}}'.

role.description: Role of the organization relative to the presentation. Only 'primary' has behavior: it selects the primary organization (cover and section logo, the 'socials' header/footer field, and the 'organization.<field>' built-ins). When no organization has role 'primary', the first one is primary. 'partner', 'client', 'sponsor' and 'host' are descriptive labels that change nothing.

socials.description: Optional social media handles or URLs for the organization. The primary organization's socials render in header/footer zones that set socials: true; otherwise they are authoring metadata.

Speaker.description: A person presenting the deck. A speaker is drawn only through built-in variables ('{{speaker.name}}' inside any string, a header or footer text included, and 'var:speaker.photo' as a whole image field). No layout, cover or bio slide places a speaker on its own. See docs/templates-and-variables.md.

id.description: Stable identifier for the speaker. Must be unique among speakers (a duplicate is a validation error). Addresses this speaker in built-in variables as 'speaker.<id>.<field>', such as '{{speaker.alice.title}}'.

name.description: Display name. Built-in variable 'speaker.name' (first speaker) or 'speaker.<id>.name'; every name is listed by 'speakers'.

title.description: Role or title. Built-in variable 'speaker.title' (or 'speaker.<id>.title'), for example in a footer text of '{{speaker.name}}, {{speaker.title}}'.

photo.description: Source for the speaker's headshot image. Accepts an HTTPS URL, data URI, relative path (resolved against the OPF file location), local path, or 'asset:<id>' reference. Common formats are JPG or PNG; SVG is not appropriate for photographic content. Never drawn automatically: it is the built-in image variable 'speaker.photo' (or 'speaker.<id>.photo'), placed with 'var:speaker.photo' in a slide's image field. It also round-trips through PPTX provenance.

email.description: Contact email. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'speaker.email'.

phone.description: Contact phone number for the speaker. E.164 format is recommended. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'speaker.phone'.

bio.description: Short biographical paragraph. Never drawn automatically; available as the built-in variable 'speaker.bio', for a bio or 'about the speaker' slide you write.
examples: Alice leads engineering at Acme, where she's spent the last six years scaling distributed systems from prototype to billions of requests per day. Previously, she was a staff engineer at Google.

organizationId.description: Reference to an Organization.id in organization; it must name an existing organization (a validation error otherwise). Attribution metadata for hosts: no engine draws it or changes which organization is primary because of it.

socials.description: Optional social media handles or URLs for the speaker. Authoring metadata only: nothing draws speaker socials and there is no built-in variable for them (the 'socials' header/footer field draws the primary organization's socials).

Socials.description: Social media handles or URLs, keyed by platform. The keys are an engine vocabulary validated directly (no catalog lookup): engines link a handle with the platform's URL pattern and handle prefix (spec/reference/engine-vocabularies.json). Each value is a string, either a full URL or a platform handle (e.g., '@acme'). Brand colours and icons are catalog display metadata for authoring UIs; engines render the profile URL, not icons or brand colours. Used both for organization and speaker records.

additionalProperties.description: Handle or URL for the platform identified by the property key.

propertyNames.description: Platform key, one of the engine's social platforms.

Design.description: Visual design system applied to the presentation; individual slides may override fields via Slide.design.

theme.description: Theme for the deck: a themes reference, a bare id ('minimal') or 'name:id' ('acme:brand'). The theme supplies the default colour scheme, font scheme, background and dimensions; design.colorScheme, design.fontScheme, design.background and design.dimensions override it field by field. A reference that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference and engines use the engine default theme.

colorScheme.description:
Color scheme for the presentation. Accepts two forms:
- A colorSchemes reference: a bare id ('cool-horizon') or 'name:id' ('acme:ocean').
- Object form: a ColorScheme with an optional 'id' reference as the base plus slot/role overrides. Without 'id', the overrides apply on top of the engine default colour scheme.

Without either, the theme's colorScheme applies, then the engine default colour scheme.

fontScheme.description:
Font scheme for heading, body, accent, and code text. Accepts two forms:
- A fontSchemes reference: a bare id ('aptos') or 'name:id' ('acme:inter').
- Object form: a FontScheme with an optional 'id' reference as the base plus pair/role overrides.

Without either, the theme's fontScheme applies, then the engine default font scheme.

dimensions.description: Slide dimensions and aspect ratio. String shorthand such as 'widescreen' is equivalent to { preset: 'widescreen' }.

background.description: Default slide background applied across the deck unless overridden on a slide (slides.N.design.background); the resolved theme's background is the fallback. A background is the only canvas fill and never moves content. String shorthand accepts theme slots ('light1', 'light2', 'dark1', 'dark2'), hex colors, or an image source starting with 'asset:', 'https://', 'data:', './' or '../' (a cover image); object forms support theme, solid, gradient, image, or pattern fills.

logo.description: Which logo covers, section dividers and picture bullets draw. Logos live on the organization (Organization.logo); without this field covers and sections draw the primary organization's full logo and picture bullets its icon. A logo reference overrides that: 'var:organization.beta.logo' draws organization beta's logo, and a reference that names a shape ('var:organization.logo.wordmark') draws that shape everywhere this field applies. false draws no logo. A slide's design.logo overrides the deck's; absence inherits. An override naming an organization without a logo draws nothing (validation warns). Placement (reference engines, vetoable): on a cover or section slide (no body payload on a heading-only layout such as title, title-subtitle or section-divider, or no layout) the logo is drawn at the top-left of the free area, inside the slide padding and below any header furniture, in a box 56 reference pixels tall and at most four times as wide; the tag/title/subtitle group then centers in the remaining span. Content slides never get an automatic logo; a header or footer zone places one with image: 'var:organization.logo.icon'. composeSlide returns the cover box as geometry.logo.

watermark.description: Optional decorative watermark applied across slides: an image or a text stamp, in the fixed frame and at the opacity described on Watermark. Use false to suppress an inherited watermark in slide-level design; a string or Asset is the image at opacity 0.08.

header.description: Repeated header furniture rendered outside the main slide content. Use false to suppress an inherited header.

footer.description: Repeated footer furniture rendered outside the main slide content. Use false to suppress an inherited footer.

titleAlignment.description: Default horizontal alignment for title placeholders in resolved layouts. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.titleAlignment, then the layout record's design.titleAlignment, then the engine default.

contentAlignment.description: Default horizontal alignment for body/content regions in resolved layouts. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.contentAlignment, then the layout record's design.contentAlignment, then the engine default. A cover's tag and subtitle follow titleAlignment unless the slide's own design sets contentAlignment.

contentBox.description: Whether body/content regions are rendered inside a visible card or surface. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.contentBox, then the layout record's design.contentBox, then the engine default.

contentDirection.description: Axis along which parallel body content is arranged: 'vertical' is a column, 'horizontal' a row. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.contentDirection, then the layout record's design.contentDirection. On a slide with a template layout (OPF 0.19) it turns every flowing region of the slide into one row or one column, below the slide's own composition.mode, columns and weights, which arrange its first primary flowing region. On an automatic slide (and a 0.18 record) it sets the root arrangement mode when no composition.mode is set on the slide or on its layout record. Promoted regions (left, top:left, ...) keep their explicit geometry and nested groups keep their own composition.

chartPrimary.description: Where the primary chart sits relative to supporting content. Effective value: slide design, then deck design, then the layout record's design.chartPrimary. It applies to automatic slides (and 0.18 records) only; a template layout says the same with its regions (chart-beside). When the slide has no promoted regions and no composition.mode of its own, and its root nodes mix at least one chart with other content, the first chart becomes a primary track and the other nodes form one synthetic sub-grid: 'left'/'right' is a two-track row and 'top'/'bottom' a two-track column, weighted 3:2 in favor of the chart; explicit root columns and weights are ignored while it applies. 'none' (the default) keeps the ordinary automatic grid with equal weight. It is shorthand for a placeholder group (layout.schema.json PlaceholderGroup): the slide composes exactly as on a layout record whose root composition is that weighted row or column and whose placeholders are the chart and one automatic group of the other content, and while it applies it replaces the layout record's own placeholder groups as well.

imageFit.description: Default fit of image blocks (and Slide.image) that set no fit of their own: 'cover' fills the frame and crops what overflows around the block's focus, 'contain' shows the whole picture centered in the frame, 'stretch' scales it to the frame exactly. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.imageFit, then the layout record's design.imageFit, then 'cover'. Backgrounds set their own fit.

listBullet.description: Marker style for items and bullets lists. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the theme's design.listBullet, then the layout record's design.listBullet, then 'character'. 'character' (the default) draws the glyph marker. 'image' draws the primary organization's icon logo (or the organization and shape design.logo names; the onDark value on dark backgrounds) as a picture bullet: a square of the marker's font size whose bottom sits on the marker baseline, so list geometry does not change. Without a logo the glyph is drawn and the engine reports unresolved-content at this field.

mirror.description: Draw the slide's template layout mirrored (OPF 0.19): each row's cells and the column sizes reversed, so a 'beside' layout puts its picture, chart or table at the end. Logical: a right-to-left deck mirrors on top. Binding and reading order do not change. Effective value: the slide's design, then the deck's design, then the layout record's design.mirror, then false. Slides without a template layout ignore it.

ColorScheme.description:
Color palette used by the design system. Every slot and role is a hex color ('#RGB', '#RRGGBB' or '#RRGGBBAA'); a color-scheme name or a 'var:<id>' reference is not valid here, because those resolve through the scheme. The slot fields (accent1-accent6, dark1, dark2, light1, light2, hyperlink, followedHyperlink) mirror color-scheme.schema.json (https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-color-scheme/v1) so library records and inline OPF overrides are interchangeable on those fields.

Two parallel models are supported and may be mixed:
- OOXML slots - the 12-slot PowerPoint theme model that round-trips directly to OOXML. Use these for full control over the palette as PowerPoint sees it.
- Abstract roles (primary, secondary, accent, background, surface, text, textSecondary) - OPF-specific semantic aliases the engine maps onto the OOXML slots. Convenient for inline overrides without thinking in slot numbers; not part of the catalog record schema.

In design.colorScheme, 'id' resolves a colorSchemes record as the base; slot and role overrides on the same object take precedence over the resolved scheme. The string form of design.colorScheme is equivalent to setting only 'id'.

id.description: Colour-scheme reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved as the base; slot and role overrides on the surrounding ColorScheme object take precedence over the resolved scheme.

accent1.description: Accent 1 color (hex). Mirrors the OOXML accent1 slot.

accent2.description: Accent 2 color (hex). Mirrors the OOXML accent2 slot.

accent3.description: Accent 3 color (hex). Mirrors the OOXML accent3 slot.

accent4.description: Accent 4 color (hex). Mirrors the OOXML accent4 slot.

accent5.description: Accent 5 color (hex). Mirrors the OOXML accent5 slot.

accent6.description: Accent 6 color (hex). Mirrors the OOXML accent6 slot.

dark1.description: Dark 1 color (hex). Typically the deepest neutral; OOXML dark1.

dark2.description: Dark 2 color (hex). Secondary dark; OOXML dark2.

light1.description: Light 1 color (hex). Typically the slide canvas; OOXML lt1.

light2.description: Light 2 color (hex). Secondary light surface; OOXML lt2.

hyperlink.description: Hyperlink color (hex). OOXML hlink. Link runs with no color of their own are drawn underlined in it, in the preview and in PowerPoint, unless it has under 4.5:1 contrast against the slide background, then in the slide text color.

primary.description: Abstract role: primary brand color (hex). The engine maps this onto an OOXML accent slot when serializing.

accent.description: Abstract role: accent color used for highlights and emphasis (hex).

background.description: Abstract role: default slide background color (hex), used when the design names no single-color background (and for gradient and picture backgrounds). Overrides light1 as that default.

surface.description: Abstract role: color for elevated surfaces such as cards and panels (hex). Overrides the default of light2 (dark2 on a dark slide).

text.description: Abstract role: primary body text color (hex). Overrides dark1 on a light slide only; a dark slide always uses light1.

textSecondary.description: Abstract role: secondary or muted text color used for captions and supporting copy (hex). Overrides the default of dark2 (light2 on a dark slide).

FontScheme.description:
Typography selections used by the design system. The pair fields (major, minor) and refinement fields (type, app, languageFamily) mirror font-scheme.schema.json (https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-font-scheme/v1) so library records and inline OPF overrides are interchangeable on those fields.

Two parallel models are supported and may be mixed:
- OOXML pairs (major, minor) - heading and body family names that round-trip directly to PowerPoint majorFont/minorFont entries.
- Abstract roles (heading, body, accent, code) - OPF-specific font family names the engine maps onto the OOXML pair when serializing. Convenient for inline overrides and for adding accent/code roles that don't have a direct OOXML slot. Catalog records may also carry 'code' (for example the consolas and courier-new records); heading, body and accent are not part of the catalog record schema. A role is a family name only: weight, style and tracking come from the text styles, and PowerPoint has no numeric weight.

In design.fontScheme, 'id' resolves a fontSchemes record as the base; pair and role overrides on the same object take precedence over the resolved scheme. The string form of design.fontScheme is equivalent to setting only 'id'.

id.description: Font-scheme reference (a bare id or 'name:id') resolved as the base; field overrides on the surrounding FontScheme object take precedence over the resolved scheme.

major.description: Heading (major) font family — mirrors the OOXML majorFont entry. Pairs with 'minor'.

minor.description: Body (minor) font family — mirrors the OOXML minorFont entry. Pairs with 'major'.

eastAsian.description: East Asian script fonts. Maps to the OOXML a:ea element of majorFont (major) and minorFont (minor), and to run-level a:ea. When set, they fill the eastAsian slot for every language; when omitted, the slot comes from this scheme's own major/minor when languageFamily is 'ea' and the scheme's languages list is empty or names the presentation language, then from the presentation language's font scheme for East Asian languages, and otherwise from the latin (major/minor) families. A missing 'major' or 'minor' falls back to the other.

major.description: Heading (major) eastAsian font family — mirrors majorFont a:ea.

minor.description: Body (minor) eastAsian font family — mirrors minorFont a:ea.

complexScript.description: Complex-script fonts (for example Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and Thai). Maps to the OOXML a:cs element of majorFont (major) and minorFont (minor), and to run-level a:cs. When set, they fill the complexScript slot for every language; when omitted, the slot comes from this scheme's own major/minor when languageFamily is 'cs' and the scheme's languages list is empty or names the presentation language, then from the presentation language's font scheme for complex-script languages, and otherwise from the latin (major/minor) families. A missing 'major' or 'minor' falls back to the other.

major.description: Heading (major) complexScript font family — mirrors majorFont a:cs.

minor.description: Body (minor) complexScript font family — mirrors minorFont a:cs.

type.description: High-level typographic class of the scheme.

app.description: Target application this font pairing is intended for. Metadata for pickers and catalog filters: no engine changes its output by it.

languageFamily.description: Font-language family this scheme is intended for: 'latin' for Latin-script content, 'ea' (or 'eastAsian', the same value) for East Asian scripts, 'cs' (or 'complexScript', the same value) for Complex Scripts. The long names match the 'eastAsian' and 'complexScript' slot keys; the short names match the OOXML a:ea and a:cs elements; core reads both spellings as one value. As the design font scheme, an 'ea'/'eastAsian' or 'cs'/'complexScript' scheme also fills that script slot with its own major/minor families when its languages list is empty or names the presentation language.

heading.description: Abstract role: font family name used for slide titles and headings. Maps onto the OOXML major slot when serializing.

body.description: Abstract role: font family name used for body copy. Maps onto the OOXML minor slot when serializing.

accent.description: Abstract role: font family name used for accent text. When set, the slide tag (eyebrow) and the quote body use this family instead of the body and heading families; nothing else changes. resolveFontFamilies() returns it as accent only when the scheme defines it. No direct OOXML slot: PPTX export writes it on those runs, and the theme fonts stay major/minor.

code.description: Abstract role: monospaced font family name used for code blocks and for inline code runs (TextRun.code). No direct OOXML slot. Resolution: this override, then the resolved font-scheme record's 'code' (for example Consolas for the consolas scheme), then the engine fallback Roboto Mono. Heading and body families are never used as the code fallback.

SlideDesign.description: A slide's design: every Design field except dimensions. A PPTX has one slide size, so the size is set once, on the deck's design.dimensions (or its theme), and a slide's design cannot set it. A slide-level theme whose resolved dimensions differ from the deck's is a validate warning (opf/slide-theme-dimensions); exporting such a deck to PPTX fails with mixed-slide-dimensions.

DimensionPreset.description: Named preset; sets aspect ratio and physical size. 16:9 ('widescreen'): 13.333 x 7.5 in, PowerPoint's Widescreen. 4:3 ('standard'): 10 x 7.5 in. 16:10: 10 x 6.25 in. letter (11 x 8.5 in) and a4 (11.69 x 8.27 in) are paper sizes, not PowerPoint's Letter Paper or A4 Paper. 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 are 7.5 in on the short edge.

Dimensions.description: Slide dimensions: a preset, or custom inches that override it. PowerPoint's Letter Paper (10 x 7.5 in), A4 Paper (10.8333 x 7.5 in) and On-screen Show (16:9) (10 x 5.625 in) are not OPF presets; use widthInches and heightInches. docs/slide-sizes.md compares every preset.

widthInches.description: Custom slide width in inches; overrides the preset width when provided.

heightInches.description: Custom slide height in inches; overrides the preset height when provided.

ThemeBackgroundSlot.description: PowerPoint theme-controlled slide background slot from the active color scheme. These are slots, not assumptions about actual colors: light1 is usually white and dark1 is usually black by convention, but the color scheme controls the real values.

HexColor.description: Hex color shorthand accepted by selected string fields.

ColorRef.description:
A color value or reference, enforced on styled table cell fill and text colors, cell border colors, solid background colors, gradient stop colors and pattern foreground and background colors. Three forms:
- Literal hex: '#RGB', '#RRGGBB', or '#RRGGBBAA'.
- Color-scheme name, resolved through the effective color scheme after design resolution: an OOXML slot ('accent1'-'accent6', 'dark1', 'dark2', 'light1', 'light2', 'hyperlink', 'followedHyperlink') or an abstract role ('primary', 'secondary', 'accent', 'background', 'surface', 'surfaceAlt', 'text', 'textSecondary'). Roles resolve through the same role-to-slot mapping engines already apply to color schemes. 'surfaceAlt' has no slot: it is the alternate surface of banded table rows, derived from 'surface' and 'text' (the surface mixed a tenth of the way towards the text color, further when needed, so it always differs visibly from 'surface' and keeps 4.5:1 text contrast; core surfaceAltColor).
- Variable reference: 'var:<id>' into the top-level variables map.

Names keep content theme-portable: re-theming the deck updates every named reference, where a literal hex stays frozen. Unknown 'var:' ids produce a validation warning, never an error, and engines fall back to their default text color. TextRun.color documents the same three forms but remains an open string so imported decks with unrecognized run colors stay valid; validators warn there instead of erroring.

Variables.description: Named variables, keyed by stable kebab-case id. A variable is a typed, named value the deck declares once and uses in many places: a color ('var:<id>' in color fields, the original use), or content that fills a template (text, number, date, image, url, list). Content is referenced inline as '{{<id>}}' inside any string, or whole as 'var:<id>' in a field of the matching type; '\{{' writes a literal '{{'. A hex string is shorthand for a color variable. A variable with no 'value' is unfilled: expected in a template (root 'template': true), an error in a normal deck. Engines resolve variables with resolveVariables() before composing, rendering or exporting, so a template plus its values previews and exports exactly like the equivalent hand-written deck. Read-only built-in variables come from the deck's own metadata and use dotted names that a user id can never take: 'deck.name', 'deck.description', 'deck.author', 'speaker.name|title|email|phone|bio|photo' (first speaker), 'speakers' (every speaker's name, a list), 'organization.name|legalName|tagline|domain|email|phone' (primary organization), and 'speaker.<id>.<field>' / 'organization.<id>.<field>' by id. They are written the same two ways ('{{speaker.name}}', 'var:speaker.photo'), are never declared, and an unknown built-in path is a validation error; a known one with no source value resolves to nothing with a warning. The id 'speakers' is reserved. Three built-ins are slide-scoped and written only as inline tokens: '{{slide.number}}' (the displayed slide number after pagination), '{{slide.section}}' (the slide's section) and '{{deck.slideCount}}' (the number of slides after pagination). resolveVariables() leaves them as written; they resolve per slide as it is composed (resolveSlideVariables(), and header/footer text in layoutFurniture()), so every 'slide.' name is reserved and 'var:slide.*' or 'var:deck.slideCount' is a validation error. Organization logos are slide-scoped whole-field images: 'var:organization.logo', 'var:organization.logo.<shape>' (full, stacked, icon, wordmark), 'var:organization.<id>.logo' and 'var:organization.<id>.logo.<shape>' resolve per slide to the onLight or onDark asset for its background. See docs/templates-and-variables.md.

Variable.description: A single named variable: a hex string (shorthand for a color variable) or an object whose 'type' is color, text, number, date, image, url or list. 'value' is the current value and is optional: a variable with no value is unfilled, which a template allows and a normal deck does not. 'example' only illustrates the slot (fill forms, template previews) and never reaches output.

type.description: Variable kind. One of color, text, number, date, image, url or list.

value.description: Hex color this variable resolves to.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

label.description: Optional short human label for forms and fill panels.

description.description: Optional prose describing what the variable is for, surfaced by pickers, fill forms and agents.

example.description: Illustrative color shown in fill forms and used when a template is previewed with examples. Never written to output.

ColorVariable.description: A named color. Content color fields reference it as 'var:<id>'. Colors resolve at render time through the ordinary color-reference path, so a color variable keeps working as before.

type.description: Variable kind. One of color, text, number, date, image, url or list.

value.description: Text this variable resolves to: a plain string, or TextRun[] for rich text.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

label.description: Optional short human label for forms and fill panels.

description.description: Optional prose describing what the variable is for, surfaced by pickers, fill forms and agents.

example.description: Illustrative text shown in fill forms and used when a template is previewed with examples. Never written to output.

TextVariable.description: Text content. Plain string or rich TextRun[]. Insert it inline as '{{<id>}}' inside any string (rich text is flattened to plain text there), or reference it whole as 'var:<id>' in a field that accepts string or TextRun[] (the rich runs are kept).

type.description: Variable kind. One of color, text, number, date, image, url or list.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

label.description: Optional short human label for forms and fill panels.

description.description: Optional prose describing what the variable is for, surfaced by pickers, fill forms and agents.

example.description: Illustrative number shown in fill forms and used when a template is previewed with examples. Never written to output.

format.description: Display pattern used by '{{<id>}}' (the shared NumberFormat syntax). A literal prefix, a numeric part of '#', '0', ',' and '.', and a literal suffix. '0' pads digits, '#' is optional, ',' groups thousands, digits after '.' fix the decimals ('0' required, '#' optional), and a '%' in the suffix scales by 100. English separators only. Absent: the shortest decimal form.

NumberVariable.description: A number. '{{<id>}}' inserts it as text using 'format'; 'var:<id>' as a whole field supplies the number itself (chart values, font sizes).

NumberFormat.description: Number display pattern, shared by NumberVariable.format, data column formats (DataColumn.format) and table cell formats (StyledTableCell.format). An optional literal prefix, a numeric part of '#', '0', ',' and '.', and an optional literal suffix. '0' pads digits, '#' is optional, ',' groups thousands, digits after '.' fix the decimals ('0' required, '#' optional), and a '%' in the prefix or suffix multiplies the value by 100. English separators only. A format applies only to number values; strings, booleans, null and rich runs display unchanged. A column or cell format that is not a valid pattern is a 'number-format-invalid' error. The PPTX export writes it as the equivalent Excel number format code.

type.description: Variable kind. One of color, text, number, date, image, url or list.

value.description: ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) this variable resolves to.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

label.description: Optional short human label for forms and fill panels.

description.description: Optional prose describing what the variable is for, surfaced by pickers, fill forms and agents.

example.description: Illustrative ISO date shown in fill forms and used when a template is previewed with examples. Never written to output.

format.description: Date display pattern, the same LDML-style tokens as header/footer dateFormat: yyyy, yy, MMMM, MMM, MM, M, dd, d, EEEE, EEE and quoted literals. English names. Default 'MMMM d, yyyy'.

DateVariable.description: A calendar date as an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string. No time zone and no clock are involved. '{{<id>}}' inserts it formatted with 'format'.

type.description: Variable kind. One of color, text, number, date, image, url or list.

value.description: Image source this variable resolves to.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

label.description: Optional short human label for forms and fill panels.

description.description: Optional prose describing what the variable is for, surfaced by pickers, fill forms and agents.

example.description: Illustrative image source shown in fill forms and used when a template is previewed with examples. Never written to output.

ImageVariable.description: An image source: any Asset (an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, relative or local path, or an object with src, alt and metadata). Reference it whole as 'var:<id>' in an image, asset or src field; '{{<id>}}' inserts the source string.

type.description: Variable kind. One of color, text, number, date, image, url or list.

value.description: Link target this variable resolves to.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

label.description: Optional short human label for forms and fill panels.

description.description: Optional prose describing what the variable is for, surfaced by pickers, fill forms and agents.

example.description: Illustrative link shown in fill forms and used when a template is previewed with examples. Never written to output.

UrlVariable.description: A link target (http, https, mailto or tel). Use it as '{{<id>}}' inside a link string or reference it whole as 'var:<id>' in a link field.

type.description: Variable kind. One of color, text, number, date, image, url or list.

required.description: Whether the variable must be filled. Defaults to true: a variable with no 'value' is unfilled, and an unfilled required variable is an error in a normal deck and expected in a template. Set false for an optional slot: an unfilled optional variable resolves to empty text (inline tokens) or the field that references it is omitted.

label.description: Optional short human label for forms and fill panels.

description.description: Optional prose describing what the variable is for, surfaced by pickers, fill forms and agents.

example.description: Illustrative entries shown in fill forms and used when a template is previewed with examples. Never written to output.

ListVariable.description: A list of strings, for bullets and list items. A whole-string array element 'var:<id>' splices every entry into the array in place; a whole field 'var:<id>' becomes the array; '{{<id>}}' joins the entries with ', ' (or the separator after a pipe: '{{<id>|; }}').

BackgroundShortcut.description: String shorthand for a background. Theme slots ('light1', 'light2', 'dark1', 'dark2') are equivalent to { type: 'theme', slot: value }; hex colors are equivalent to { type: 'solid', color: value }; an image source (starting with 'asset:', 'https://', 'data:', './' or '../') is equivalent to { type: 'image', src: value }, a cover image. Any other string is invalid.

ImageSource.description: An image source in a string shorthand: an 'asset:<id>' reference, an HTTPS URL, a data URI, or a relative path starting with './' or '../' (resolved against the OPF file location).

Background.description: Background fill applied to slides. Theme backgrounds preserve PowerPoint's color-scheme background choice; other variants represent fixed background fills.

ThemeBackground.description: Theme-controlled PowerPoint slide background. The slot is resolved through the active color scheme and remains theme-aware.

color.description: Fixed solid fill color: a hex string, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a var:<id> variable reference (a ColorRef, resolved against the effective color scheme and the deck variables). Use { type: 'theme', slot: ... } for PowerPoint's four theme-controlled background choices.

opacity.description: Background opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque).

angle.description: Gradient angle in degrees (0 = left-to-right, 90 = top-to-bottom).

stops.description: Ordered list of color stops along the gradient. A gradient needs at least two stops.

color.description: Stop color: a hex string, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a var:<id> variable reference (a ColorRef).

position.description: Stop position along the gradient, from 0 (start) to 1 (end).

opacity.description: Background opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque).

ImageBackground.description: Picture background: the image fills the whole canvas behind everything and never moves content (to push content aside, use an image block with placement). The string shorthand 'asset:x' (or any image source) is { type: 'image', src: 'asset:x' }, a cover image. Paint order: the colour scheme's default slide background, the picture, then the overlay, then furniture and content.

src.description: Source for the background image: an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, or a relative path resolved against the OPF file location.

alt.description: Alternative text. A background with alt is meaningful: PowerPoint export draws it as a full-slide picture at the back that carries the text, so screen readers see it. Without alt it is decorative and exports as the native slide background; the alt text of a referenced asset does not count, so a background is decorative unless it says otherwise.

fit.description: How the picture fills the canvas: 'cover' fills it and crops what overflows around focus; 'contain' shows the whole picture centered over the colour scheme's default background; 'stretch' scales it to the canvas exactly; 'tile' repeats it at its own size from the top-left corner. Default 'cover'.

focus.description: Point of the picture to keep in view when 'cover' crops it. Ignored by the other fits.

opacity.description: Picture opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque); the overlay keeps its own opacity. Default 1.

recolor.description: Grayscale or duotone treatment of the picture's pixels, as on an image block: recolor and opacity apply to the pixels, then the overlay is drawn above.

overlay.description: Scrim over the whole picture or a band along one edge (edge, size), beneath furniture and content, for example to keep a title readable over a busy photo.

ImageFocus.description: A point of a picture as fractions of its width and height, from the top-left corner. A cover fit centers this point in the frame as far as the picture still covers the frame, so it always stays in view: { x: 0.5, y: 0.5 } (the default) is a center crop, { x: 0, y: 0 } keeps the top-left corner.

Overlay.description: Solid scrim over a picture: the whole frame in the frame's shape, or a band along one edge. Shared by image backgrounds and image blocks. Drawn directly above its picture and beneath headings and content; PowerPoint export writes one native shape above the picture.

color.description: Overlay fill color: a hex color (eight-digit hex keeps its alpha), a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference.

edge.description: Cover only a band along this edge of the frame, for example a caption strip. Backgrounds and rectangle image frames only; on another shape the overlay is not drawn and composition reports unsupported-image-treatment. Omit to cover the whole frame. In a right-to-left deck 'left' and 'right' are the start and end sides.

size.description: Band share of the frame for an edge overlay. Default 0.3. Ignored without edge.

ImagePlacement.description: Bleeds an image block to one edge of the slide: the image takes a band along that edge, edge to edge, and the headings and other content compose in the rest of the slide at the normal padding. Only top-level blocks (slides.N.blocks.I) can be placed, at most one per edge; a layout's image placeholder may carry the same placement for the slide's image. Bands are taken in block order, each spanning the free area left by earlier ones. Placement is the only mechanism that moves content aside; a background never does. A slide whose only body is placed images is composed like a cover: its headings center in the free area. In a right-to-left deck 'left' is the start side, drawn at the right.

edge.description: The slide edge the image bleeds to.

size.description: Share of the slide width (left, right) or height (top, bottom) given to the band. Default 0.5.

inset.description: Draw the frame inside the slide padding on every side of the band, like a card, instead of edge to edge. Default false.

ImageBorder.description: Solid line along the image frame's shape, centered on the outline with a miter join, like a native picture line. A thick dark border on a rounded portrait frame gives a device bezel.

color.description: Line color: a hex color, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference.

width.description: Line width in reference pixels at a 720-pixel short edge. 0 removes the line.

oneOf.description: Replace each pixel with its luminance, exported as native a:grayscl.
Duotone: map each pixel's luminance linearly from dark to light, exported as native a:duotone.

ImageRecolor.description: Color treatment for the image pixels. Luminance uses Rec. 601 weights (0.299, 0.587, 0.114) on sRGB values.

preset.description: Pattern preset or engine-defined pattern id. DrawingML preset names (ECMA-376 ST_PresetPatternVal, for example pct5, ltHorz, wdUpDiag) are portable: PPTX export writes them as native pattern fills and import returns the same name. Engine-defined ids are renderer-specific; the legacy preview id diagStripe remains accepted and exports as wdUpDiag.

foregroundColor.description: Foreground color for the pattern: a hex string, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a var:<id> variable reference (a ColorRef).

backgroundColor.description: Background color behind the pattern: a hex string, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a var:<id> variable reference (a ColorRef).

opacity.description: Background opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque).

OrganizationLogo.description: An organization's logo in up to four shapes. Each shape is a path or Asset, or { onLight, onDark } for the two backgrounds. A missing shape falls back to full, and full to the first defined of wordmark, stacked and icon; within a shape a missing onLight or onDark uses the other. Shapes are placed with slide-scoped references such as 'var:organization.logo.icon'.

full.description: The full logo (lockup): mark and name side by side. Drawn on cover and section slides, and placed by 'var:organization.logo'.

stacked.description: The stacked lockup: mark above the name, for portrait or square slots. Placed by 'var:organization.logo.stacked'.

icon.description: The mark or symbol without the name, for tight spaces such as header and footer zones and picture bullets. Placed by 'var:organization.logo.icon'.

wordmark.description: The name set in the brand's lettering, without the mark. Placed by 'var:organization.logo.wordmark'.

LogoSource.description: One logo shape: a path or Asset for every background, or { onLight, onDark }. onLight is drawn on light backgrounds (usually dark artwork) and onDark on dark backgrounds (usually light artwork), by each slide's background; a missing one uses the other.

onLight.description: The logo for light backgrounds, usually dark artwork.

onDark.description: The logo for dark backgrounds, usually light or white artwork.

Watermark.description: Decorative watermark: an image ('src') or a text stamp ('text'), exactly one of the two, with its opacity. An image is drawn once per slide, contained and centered in a fixed frame (the middle 40% of the slide width and height, from 30% to 70% on each axis). A text watermark is one line of text in the heading font and the theme text color at the given opacity, centered on the slide and rotated 30 degrees counterclockwise (rising to the right), sized to span at most 70% of the slide width and at most 30% of the shorter slide edge in height; it is drawn behind the slide content and above the background. There is no option to move, scale, rotate or tile either form. PPTX export writes one native picture (image) or one native text box (text) per slide with the opacity as alpha, and import restores the watermark. A string or Asset (no opacity) is the image watermark at opacity 0.08. A watermark object needs opacity and exactly one of src and text; use a plain string or Asset for an image at the default opacity. Use design.watermark = false to disable an inherited watermark.

src.description: Source for the watermark image: an 'asset:<id>' reference, HTTPS URL, data URI, relative path or local path, as for Asset.src. Exactly one of src and text is set.

text.description: Text for a text watermark, such as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL; line breaks are drawn as spaces. Exactly one of src and text is set.

opacity.description: Watermark opacity from 0 (fully transparent) to 1 (fully opaque).

HeaderFooter.description: Repeated header or footer content split into left, center, and right zones. Header/footer content is slide furniture, separate from the main slide content payloads.

HeaderFooterItem.description: One header/footer zone. Every configured field renders, side by side in one row in the order image, text, socials, date (mirrored in a right-to-left deck), aligned to the zone's edge (left, center or right) and vertically centered on each other; a line break inside text or socials ('\n') stacks lines within that part. When the parts are wider than the zone their text wraps, and a row that cannot fit even so is reported as overflow. Generated values such as the slide number, the slide count, the section, the organization or the speaker are variables inside text ('{{slide.number}} / {{deck.slideCount}}', '{{organization.name}}'), so one text writes several values in the author's order. An organization logo is image: 'var:organization.logo.icon'. See docs/templates-and-variables.md.

text.description: Text rendered in this zone. Variables resolve inside it like any string: deck-wide ones ('{{organization.name}}', '{{speaker.name}}, {{speaker.title}}', '{{customer}}') before composition, and the slide-scoped built-ins '{{slide.number}}', '{{slide.section}}' and '{{deck.slideCount}}' for each slide as it is laid out. Each '{{slide.number}}' is a live slide-number field: PPTX export writes it as a native field when its value fits within one accepted text line, and as static text with a diagnostic otherwise. '{{deck.slideCount}}' is fixed text, because PowerPoint has no slide-count field. Write '\{{' for literal braces.

image.description: Image rendered first in this zone's row, such as a logo, partner mark, certification badge, or icon: a path, URL or Asset, or an organization logo reference ('var:organization.logo.icon', 'var:organization.<id>.logo.wordmark'), which resolves for each slide's background (onLight or onDark).

date.description: true renders the current date: the renderer or exporter must be given an explicit ISO date by its host (core never reads a clock). PPTX export writes a native date field only for a supported dateFormat whose complete value fits within one accepted text line; otherwise it writes static text with a diagnostic. Native PowerPoint refresh and save/reopen compatibility require separate verification. A string is fixed: with dateFormat it must be an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date and is formatted; without dateFormat it is literal text rendered as written.

dateFormat.description: Date pattern for date. Tokens: yyyy (2026), yy (26), MMMM (April), MMM (Apr), MM (04), M (4), dd (09), d (9), EEEE (Thursday), EEE (Thu). Text in single quotes and other non-letter characters are literal. Month and weekday names are English, independent of host locale. Defaults to "M/d/yyyy" for a current date. PPTX export writes a native current-date field only when its complete value fits within one accepted text line and the pattern matches a PowerPoint en-US date field ('M/d/yyyy'; 'EEEE, MMMM d, yyyy'; 'd MMMM yyyy'; 'MMMM d, yyyy'; 'd-MMM-yy'; 'MMMM yy'; 'MMM-yy'). Other patterns and wrapped fields export as static text with a diagnostic. Full provenance can recover generated-date intent from unchanged supported wrapped dates on OPF reimport; the existing PPTX text remains static.

socials.description: Whether to render the primary organization's social profiles from organization.socials, one line per platform in key order. A handle is formatted through the platform's socialPlatforms record (companyUrlPattern, else profileUrlPattern, else baseUrl, with handlePrefix stripped) and shown as that profile URL without its 'https://' scheme; a value that is already a URL is shown without an 'https://' scheme; an unknown platform key shows the raw value. Exporters link each line to its full URL when one exists. Speaker socials are not rendered by this field.

Slide.description: A single slide. Content can be authored as a full-slide root payload, or inside promoted named region keys such as 'left', 'center+right', and 'top:left'.

id.description: Optional stable identifier for the slide within the document. Use when another system needs to reference a slide across edits, comments, generation state, exports, or narrative tooling. Slide order is defined by the slides array, so simple decks may omit this.

type.description: Optional full-slide content kind. When omitted, engines infer the kind from root payload fields.

beat.description: Optional reference to one or more beats of the deck's narrative (each value is the id of a beat in the narrative record that the root 'narrative' resolves to). A single string declares the slide's primary beat; an array declares that one slide covers multiple beats. Declares the slide's role in the story arc; does not constrain ordering or structure. Core validate warns about a beat id the resolved narrative does not define, and reports a beat that no slide references. Slides without a beat are valid; multiple slides may share a beat.

layout.description: Optional layout: a layouts reference, a bare id ('pillars') or 'name:id' ('acme:hero'), or 'auto'. When omitted or 'auto', the slide is composed with no layout record: engines arrange title, subtitle, tag and content automatically, a slide with no body payload is a cover (vertically centered), and design hints apply; there is no finding. 'auto' is reserved, so no catalog may define a layout of that id, and opf format drops it. A layout is a grid template (layout.schema.json): the slide's content stays flat and binds to the layout's regions by reading order, role and kind, a block may pin itself to a region with 'region', and an empty region collapses. A reference that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference (and the 'unresolved-reference' diagnostic of resolveSlideContext), the slide composes automatically, and a strict export fails. A layout id of the 0.18 default catalog that 0.19 no longer has is such a reference: 0.19 has no migration path for layouts. A layout never changes what a slide contains, and engines never substitute a different layout.

title.description: Slide-level title content. When the resolved layout exposes a 'title' placeholder, the engine renders this value there. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored word, bold, a link, a citation or footnote marker); the heading keeps its size and fitting rules either way, and run colors resolve like body text.

subtitle.description: Slide-level subtitle or supporting line. When the resolved layout exposes a 'subtitle' placeholder, the engine renders this value there. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored word, bold, a link, a citation or footnote marker); the heading keeps its size and fitting rules either way, and run colors resolve like body text.

tag.description: Small slide-level label or badge. When the resolved layout exposes a 'tag' placeholder, the engine renders this value there. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored word, bold, a link, a citation or footnote marker); the heading keeps its size and fitting rules either way, and run colors resolve like body text.

text.description: Full-slide text payload. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

items.description: Full-slide structured list payload. Presence of this field infers type 'list'. Entries are strings, TextRun[] or objects with `text`, optional `description` (supporting detail under the entry), `level` and `start`. Use `items` when entries share a shape (features, steps, options, risks) or any entry needs a `description`; use `bullets` for plain talking points. Both draw the same marker, nesting and numbering; they differ in the inferred kind and in `description`, which only `items` accepts. At slide root, multiple content payload kinds with no explicit type, blocks, or regions are accepted as shorthand for layout-agnostic blocks, so `items` next to `text` or `bullets` composes as separate blocks side by side.

bullets.description: Full-slide prose bullet payload: short talking points, each standing alone. Presence of this field infers type 'text', so it may sit beside `text` in one payload. Entries are strings, TextRun[] or objects with `text`, `level` and `start`; there is no `description` (use `items` for entries with supporting detail).

numbering.description: Number the full-slide `items` or `bullets` instead of bulleting them. A style name (arabic, roman-upper, roman-lower, alpha-upper, alpha-lower) or a Numbering object applies to every list level; an array gives one entry per level (index = level, the last entry repeats for deeper levels). Counting follows PowerPoint: consecutive entries of one level count up from its start, and an entry of a shallower level restarts the deeper levels. Absent = bullets. Valid only with `items` or `bullets`. Native PowerPoint export writes a:buAutoNum with the matching scheme and startAt; the preview draws the same numbers at the same marker geometry.

image.description: Shorthand for one image block: the picture composes as body content, like { type: 'image', image: value }, with the effective design.imageFit. A layout's image placeholder may place it along an edge (placement). For fit, focus, treatments or an explicit placement use an image block in blocks; for a full-slide picture behind the content use design.background. Presence of this field infers type 'image'.

video.description: Full-slide video source. Presence of this field infers type 'video'. Engines do not play video: the preview draws a placeholder (a play badge with the asset's title or source as its caption), and PPTX export draws the same placeholder as native shapes linked to an http(s) source, with no embedded media. Native playback is out of scope (docs/programs/release-readiness).

chart.description: Full-slide chart payload. Presence of this field infers type 'chart'.

table.description: Full-slide table payload. Presence of this field infers type 'table'.

code.description: Full-slide code payload. A string is shorthand for { "source": value }; object form carries optional syntax language and filename metadata.

metric.description: Full-slide metric payload. A string or number is shorthand for { "value": value }; object form carries optional label, description, unit, delta, trend, and sentiment metadata. Numeric values remain numbers; renderers format them for display. Presence of this field infers type 'metric'.

quote.description: Full-slide quote payload. A string is shorthand for { "text": value }; object form carries optional attribution and source metadata. Presence of this field infers type 'quote'.

timeline.description: Full-slide timeline payload. An array is shorthand for { "events": value }; object form carries optional name and description metadata. Presence of this field infers type 'timeline'.

caption.description: Caption for the slide's root image, chart, table or video payload. Valid only when the slide root holds exactly one of those payloads.

blocks.description: Layout-agnostic content blocks rendered together as a composed payload when exact placement is unspecified. At slide root, multiple content payload kinds with no explicit type, blocks, or regions are accepted as shorthand for equivalent blocks.

design.description: Slide-level design applied on top of the deck-wide design.

notes.description: Speaker notes shown in presenter view.
examples: Open with the customer story; pause for questions before moving to the architecture slide.

section.description: PowerPoint-style slide section label. Consecutive slides with the same value belong to the same section in presenter view, outlines, and PowerPoint section-aware exports. Also the slide-scoped built-in variable '{{slide.section}}', for example in a header text.

hidden.description: Whether the slide is hidden from the presented sequence. The player skips it, the PPTX export writes it as a hidden slide, and per-slide image and PDF output skips it unless the caller asks to include hidden slides (opf CLI: --include-hidden; the deck-level toSvg: the opt-in skipHidden). A slide named explicitly (opf convert --slides, toSvg with a slide number) is still rendered.

extensions.description: Custom data passthrough for agent workflows at slide scope; ignored by the engine but preserved across read/write round-trips. Use for review state, generation provenance, or authoring conventions such as { "authoring": { "locked": true } }.
