ContentPayload.description: A content leaf or recursively composed group. A group contains blocks and optional composition; it cannot mix blocks with leaf payload fields. Groups may nest up to 32 levels.

id.description: Optional stable identifier for this payload, unique among slide and payload ids in the document. Use when another system needs to address the payload across edits — patch-style agent edits, comments, review state, or generation provenance. Identity survives reordering where array indexes do not.

extensions.description: Custom data passthrough for agent workflows at payload scope; ignored by the engine but preserved across read/write round-trips.

region.description: Pin a root block (slides.N.blocks.I) to a region of the slide's template layout by name (OPF 0.19). The block goes to that region when the region exists, accepts the block's kind and has room; otherwise the pin is ignored with a warning (opf/region-unknown, opf/region-kind or opf/region-full) and the block is placed by its kind. Blocks without a pin are bound by reading order, role and kind. A pin on a nested block, or on a slide without a template layout, has no effect.

type.description: Optional content kind. When omitted, engines infer the kind from the fields present.

text.description: Text payload. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

items.description: Structured list payload (type 'list'). Each item is either a plain string, a TextRun[] rich text sequence, or a ListItem object with optional `description`. List nesting uses item.level rather than nested content payloads. Use `items` when entries share a shape or any entry needs a `description`; use `bullets` for plain talking points. Both draw the same marker, nesting and numbering. A block or region holds `items` or `bullets`, never both, and `items` cannot sit beside `text`.

examples.description: Security review ready for enterprise procurement.

bullets.description: Prose bullet payload: short talking points, each standing alone. Presence of this field infers type 'text', so it may sit beside `text` in one payload. Entries have no `description`; use `items` for entries with supporting detail.

numbering.description: Number the payload's `items` or `bullets` instead of bulleting them. A style name (arabic, roman-upper, roman-lower, alpha-upper, alpha-lower) or a Numbering object applies to every list level; an array gives one entry per level (index = level, the last entry repeats for deeper levels). Counting follows PowerPoint: consecutive entries of one level count up from its start, and an entry of a shallower level restarts the deeper levels. Absent = bullets. Valid only with `items` or `bullets`. Native PowerPoint export writes a:buAutoNum with the matching scheme and startAt; the preview draws the same numbers at the same marker geometry.

columns.description: Lay the payload's `items` or `bullets` out in columns (OPF 0.19). 'auto' tries 1, 2 then 3 equal columns at the starting text size and uses the first count at which the list fits, as long as a column stays at least a quarter of the slide wide; when none fits, the largest allowed count shrinks towards minFontSize. 1, 2 or 3 fixes the count. Column breaks fall between items (a nested item stays with its parent) and keep the columns as even as possible; numbering continues and reading order runs column by column. A lone list in a layout region with listColumns: 'auto' behaves as 'auto'.

fit.description: Image payloads only. How the picture fills its frame: 'cover' fills it and crops what overflows around focus; 'contain' shows the whole picture centered; 'stretch' scales it to the frame exactly. Default: the effective design.imageFit, else 'cover'.

focus.description: Image payloads only. Point of the picture to keep in view when 'cover' crops it. Ignored by the other fits.

aspectRatio.description: Image payloads only. Width-to-height ratio of the frame: the frame becomes the largest centered box with this ratio inside the block's region, for example 2.39 for a cinematic letterbox or 0.5 for a phone-shaped frame. shape 'circle' always uses 1.

shape.description: Image payloads only. Mask applied to the frame, exported as the picture's native preset geometry (rect, roundRect, ellipse, hexagon). 'circle' makes the frame square. Default 'rectangle'.

cornerRadius.description: Image payloads only. Corner radius for shape 'rounded' as a fraction of the frame's shorter side. Default 0.16667, PowerPoint's roundRect default.

border.description: Image payloads only. Line along the frame's shape.

opacity.description: Image payloads only. Picture opacity from 0 to 1, exported as a native alphaModFix. The border and overlay keep their own opacity. Default 1.

recolor.description: Image payloads only. Grayscale or duotone treatment of the picture's pixels.

overlay.description: Image payloads only. Scrim over the picture in the frame's shape, or a band along one edge of a rectangle frame.

placement.description: Image payloads only, and only on a top-level block (slides.N.blocks.I), at most one per edge. Bleeds the image to one slide edge; the headings and the other blocks compose in the rest of the slide.

video.description: Source for a video item. Engines do not play video: the preview draws a placeholder (a play badge with the asset's title or source as its caption), and PPTX export draws the same placeholder as native shapes linked to an http(s) source, with no embedded media. Native playback is out of scope (docs/programs/release-readiness).

chart.description: Chart payload. Presence of this field infers type 'chart'.

table.description: Table payload. Presence of this field infers type 'table'.

code.description: Code payload. A string is shorthand for { "source": value }; object form carries optional syntax language and filename metadata.
examples:
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

metric.description: Metric payload. A string or number is shorthand for { "value": value }; object form carries optional label, description, unit, delta, trend, and sentiment metadata. Numeric values remain numbers; renderers format them for display.

quote.description: Quote payload. A string is shorthand for { "text": value }; object form carries optional attribution, role, photo and source metadata.
examples: This changed how our team handles reviews.

examples.text: This changed how our team handles reviews.

timeline.description: Timeline payload ordered by narrative or chronology.

examples.description: Launch with the first operations team.

examples.name: Rollout Plan
examples.description: Major milestones for the regional rollout.

caption.description: Caption for an image, chart, table or video payload, composed inside the block's region (below the media by default). Invalid on other payload kinds and on groups.

blocks.description: Ordered children of a group. Each child is a leaf or another group.

composition.description: Arrangement within this group. Only minFontSize and overflow inherit from the parent; strict overflow cannot be weakened.

Quote.description: Quote content with optional attribution metadata. Use 'text' for the quoted text, 'attribution' for the credited person or organization, 'role' for that person's title and organization, 'photo' for their headshot and 'source' for a citation or URL. A string value in a quote field is shorthand for { "text": value }.

text.description: Quoted text: a string, or TextRun[] for inline rich text (a colored phrase, bold, a link, or a citation or footnote marker). The engine draws the surrounding quotation marks.
examples: This changed how our team handles reviews.

attribution.description: Person or organization credited for the quote. Drawn after the quote text, in the muted text color.

role.description: Title and organization of the attributed person. Drawn on its own line under the attribution; without an attribution it stands alone. It does not replace the attribution, so the person's name belongs in 'attribution'.

photo.description: Headshot of the attributed person, drawn as a circle beside the attribution and role lines (on the end side in a right-to-left deck). Give it alt text (validate's opf/missing-alt-text rule checks it). A raster photograph works best; an SVG exports as its PNG raster because the circular mask is not confirmed on SVG pictures in PowerPoint. An unresolved source draws the ordinary image placeholder.

source.description: Optional quote source, citation, or URL. Follows the attribution and role after ' - '.

Code.description: Code content with optional rendering metadata. Use 'source' for the code text, 'language' for syntax highlighting, 'filename' when the rendered block should show a file label, and 'highlight' to emphasize lines. A string value in a code field is shorthand for { "source": value }.

examples:
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

language.description: Language identifier used for syntax highlighting.

filename.description: Optional file label shown with the code block.

highlight.description: Source lines to emphasize, 1-based: each entry is a line number or an inclusive [start, end] range, so [3, [5, 7]] marks lines 3 and 5 to 7. Lines are counted by line break in 'source', so a line that wraps stays one line. Engines draw a theme-derived band behind the marked lines and dim the other lines slightly, keeping every line at least 4.5:1 against its background; PPTX export draws one native rectangle behind the line text boxes and import restores the list. A line number past the last line, or a range written end before start, gets a validation warning (code-highlight-out-of-range, code-highlight-range-reversed) and is ignored. When a code block is paginated across slides each page keeps the lines that fall on it, renumbered from 1.

Metric.description: Metric content with optional display metadata. Use 'value' for the primary value, 'label' for the metric name, 'description' for supporting context, 'unit' for a suffix/currency marker, 'delta' for change, 'trend' for direction, and 'sentiment' for whether the change is good news. A string or number value in a metric field is shorthand for { "value": value }; numeric values remain numbers and are formatted by renderers.

description.description: Optional supporting context for the metric.
examples: Median API latency across production traffic.

unit.description: Metric unit, suffix, or currency marker.

trend.description: Metric trend direction. The preview and the PowerPoint export draw an arrow beside the trend word that always points the way the trend does (up, down or flat) and colour the arrow, the trend word and the delta text by `sentiment`.

sentiment.description: Whether the change is good news. Positive draws the trend arrow and the trend and delta text in green, negative in red and neutral in the neutral text colour, each kept at 4.5:1 contrast or more against the slide background. When absent the colour follows the trend: up is positive, down is negative and flat is neutral. Set it when the direction is not the verdict, for example positive on a falling churn, cost or latency trend. The arrow always keeps the direction of `trend`. Only the trend arrow and the trend and delta text take the colour, so sentiment has no visible effect on a metric without a trend.

Timeline.description: Timeline content. An array is shorthand for { "events": value }; object form carries optional name and description metadata.

examples: Major milestones for the regional rollout.

events.description: Timeline events ordered by narrative, sequence, or chronology.

TimelineEvent.description: A single event inside a timeline content payload.

when.description: Event time, date, or sequence label. Use ISO-like values when possible, but human labels are allowed for quarters, eras, and relative milestones.

examples: Launch with the first operations team.

status.description: Progress of the event, drawn from the deck's own colors by both the SVG renderer and the PPTX exporter. Absent means no status and the event is drawn as a plain filled marker with normal text, which is also how 'done' looks. 'done' is a filled marker in the primary color with normal text. 'current' marks 'we are here': the filled marker is surrounded by a ring and the event label (`what`) is bold. 'planned' is an outlined, hollow marker (primary-color outline over the slide background) with muted secondary text. Text colors keep a 4.5:1 contrast against the slide background. In PPTX the markers are native ellipses (the ring is a second ellipse), and PPTX import restores the status the export recorded. Status describes progress only; schedule health such as at risk or blocked belongs in the event text.

ListItem.description: A flat item inside a list. Strings cover the common case, TextRun[] supports inline rich text without an object wrapper, and object form adds description and nesting depth without creating nested slide content payloads.

text.description: Text for the list item. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

description.description: Optional supporting detail for the list item. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text.
examples: Focused on activation and first-value time.

level.description: Zero-based nesting level for the list item.

start.description: Restart the list's numbering at this number for this item (counted at its level); the entries after it continue from it. Only meaningful when the payload has `numbering`. Paginated continuation pages use it to keep the numbers of the whole list.

BulletItem.description: A flat bullet item. Strings cover the common case, TextRun[] supports inline rich text without an object wrapper, and object form adds nesting depth without list-item descriptions.

text.description: Text for the bullet. Use a string for plain text or TextRun[] for inline rich text. TextRun items may be plain strings or formatted run objects.

level.description: Zero-based nesting level for the bullet.

start.description: Restart the list's numbering at this number for this bullet (counted at its level); the entries after it continue from it. Only meaningful when the payload has `numbering`. Paginated continuation pages use it to keep the numbers of the whole list.

NumberingStyle.description: A list number style: 1, 2, 3; I, II, III; i, ii, iii; A, B, C; a, b, c. Alphabetic numbering past 26 repeats the letter as PowerPoint does (aa, bb, cc). Roman numerals stop at 3999; larger values are drawn in arabic with a numbering-adapted diagnostic.

start.description: First number counted at this level. Default 1. Native PowerPoint accepts 1 to 32767.

suffix.description: Text after the number: period (1.), paren (1)) or paren-both ((1)). Default period.

NumberingSpec.description: The value of a numbering field: a style name or Numbering object for every level, or an array with one entry per level (at most 9, the native depth).

TextRun.description: A contiguous run of text. Strings cover unformatted spans; object form adds character formatting.

bold.description: Whether the run is rendered in bold.

italic.description: Whether the run is rendered in italic.

strikethrough.description: Whether the run is rendered with a strikethrough line.

color.description: Run text color. Documented forms: a hex string ('#RGB', '#RRGGBB', '#RRGGBBAA'), a color-scheme slot or role name resolved through the effective color scheme ('accent2', 'text'), or a 'var:<id>' reference into the top-level variables map. Prefer names over hex so runs survive re-theming. Any other string stays schema-valid so imported decks keep validating: validators warn and renderers fall back to the theme text color.

fontSize.description: Requested run font size in points.

fontFamily.description: Run font family override. It wins over the code font a run with 'code' takes.

code.description: Whether the run is an inline code span: it is drawn in the design's code font (design.fontScheme.code, else the resolved font scheme's code family, else Roboto Mono), unless the run names its own fontFamily. Only the font changes; there is no background, because a PPTX run cannot have one. Markdown backticks read and write code runs.

lang.description: BCP-47 language tag of the run, such as 'fr-FR' or 'ja-JP', when it differs from the deck language. It sets the proofing language (PPTX a:rPr lang) and the language the run's script fonts and glyph variants follow (for example the Japanese or the Simplified Chinese face for Han characters); without it the run follows the deck language.

link.description: URL to link the run text to: an http(s) URL, a 'mailto:' address or a 'tel:' number, without whitespace. The preview draws it as a link and PPTX export writes a native hyperlink for all three; any other scheme is not valid.

superscript.description: Whether the run is rendered as superscript.

subscript.description: Whether the run is rendered as subscript.

cite.description: One or more ids from the top-level references list that this run cites. Engines draw a superscript marker ('1', or '1,2' for several ids) directly after the run and list '<n> <reference text>' in the slide's footnote area; markers are numbered per deck in order of first use, and the same id keeps its number. An id missing from references is a validation error (cite-unknown-reference). Supported in text, bullets and list item runs, in the slide title, subtitle and tag, and in the quote text.

footnote.description: An inline note for this run, without a references entry. Engines draw a superscript marker after the run and list the note in the slide's footnote area; every footnote takes a new number in the deck's marker sequence. Supported in text, bullets and list item runs, in the slide title, subtitle and tag, and in the quote text.

Caption.description: A caption for an image, chart, table or video payload. A string or TextRun[] is the caption text placed below the media; object form adds the position and alignment.

text.description: Caption text: a string or TextRun[] for inline rich text.

position.description: Where the caption band sits inside the block's region: below the media (default) or above it. Core composition reserves the band and shrinks the media by its height.

align.description: Horizontal alignment of the caption text within the block. Defaults to left.

Reference.description: A source that runs cite with 'cite'. Cited references are listed in the footnote area of the slides that cite them, numbered per deck in order of first use; referencesSlide() builds an ordinary list slide of them.

id.description: Identifier runs cite. Unique within the references list.

text.description: The reference as it is listed: a string or TextRun[] for inline rich text.

url.description: Optional link for the reference; a references slide links its entry to it.

Chart.description: Chart content. The chart object keeps chart-specific fields together so slides and regions do not expose loose chart fields.

type.description: Chart type, an engine vocabulary validated directly (no catalog lookup): the chart types Aspose.Slides officially supports, plus 'combo' (clustered columns with line series, see 'line' and 'secondaryAxis'). Each engine maps a type to its own chart model; labels and picker groups are catalog display metadata.

data.description: Chart data. Inline data uses a tabular columns/rows shape; renderers convert rows to chart series internally. A DatasetRef ({ "dataset": "<id>" }) plots a top-level dataset instead. Data from a spreadsheet or file is imported into inline columns and rows, and its origin is recorded in data.source.

mapping.description: Optional series mapping by column name: which column is the category, which is the X column of a scatter chart, and which columns are plotted, in order. Absent keeps the positional rule (first column the category, then the X column for scatter, every other column a series).

line.description: Combo charts only (type 'combo'): the plotted series, by column name, that are drawn as lines with markers; every other plotted series is drawn as clustered columns. Absent: the last plotted series is the line. A combo chart keeps at least one column series, so a list that names every series draws the first one as columns. Column series are drawn, exported and listed in the legend first, then the line series on the primary axis, then those on the secondary axis, each in plotted order. A name that is not a column is a 'chart-mapping-unknown-column' error; a column that is not plotted is a 'chart-mapping-adapted' warning. On any other chart type it is ignored with a 'chart-option-adapted' warning.

secondaryAxis.description: Combo charts only: line series, by column name, plotted against a secondary value axis at the right of the plot. That axis has its own scale, and its tick labels use the number format of the first secondary series' column (DataColumn.format), for example '0%' for a margin. Absent: every series shares the primary value axis at the left. A name that is not a line series (see 'line') stays on the primary axis with a 'chart-mapping-adapted' warning; an unknown column is a 'chart-mapping-unknown-column' error. On any other chart type it is ignored with a 'chart-option-adapted' warning.

axisTitles.description: Optional axis titles. Absent keeps today's untitled axes. Supported on the chart types that have a category/value (or X/Y) axis pair (column, bar, line, area, scatter, and the histogram, pareto, waterfall and box-and-whisker constructs; the funnel construct takes a category title only; a combo chart also takes 'secondary' when it plots a series on the secondary axis); a title on a type without that axis (pie, doughnut, radar, treemap, map) is dropped with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic by renderers and exporters.

legend.description: Optional legend position. 'none' hides the legend. Absent keeps today's behaviour exactly (a legend at the right of multi-series charts and of pie and doughnut charts, none for single-series charts). A named position shows the legend there even for a single-series chart. Of the Office 2016 constructs only box-and-whisker takes a legend; histogram, pareto, waterfall, funnel, treemap and map drop the option with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic.

dataLabels.description: Optional data labels. true shows value labels at each type's default position, false (or absent) shows none, which is today's behaviour. Use the object form for the label content, position and separator.

alt.description: Text alternative for the chart: what the data shows (the point and the key numbers), not 'a chart' or 'bar chart'. The preview exposes it as the chart's accessible name (role img with aria-label) and the PowerPoint export writes it as the chart frame's alternative text (descr); import reads it back. An empty string marks the chart decorative, with the same meaning as an empty Asset alt, but it is a reviewed choice that opf/chart-text-alternative still reports as info (a chart almost always carries a message). When absent, validate accepts text beside the chart instead.
examples: Revenue grew from $12M in Q1 to $18M in Q2, with the steepest rise in the West region.

highlight.description: Optional emphasis: the series and/or categories that carry the message. The engines draw the highlighted marks in the deck's primary (accent) color and every other mark in a muted neutral derived from the theme (a light grey on a light chart panel, a dim grey on a dark one); there is no color field. A mark is highlighted when its series OR its category is named. Absent keeps today's colors exactly. Supported on column, bar and line charts (series and categories; on a line a category highlight marks that category's points), pie and doughnut charts (categories, one per slice), and area, scatter and radar charts (series); the histogram, pareto, waterfall, funnel, treemap, box-and-whisker, map and combo constructs drop the option with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic, as does a part the type cannot highlight. A name that matches no column or row label is a 'chart-highlight-unknown-name' error.

ChartAxisTitles.description: Titles for the axes of a chart. 'category' is the axis that carries the row labels (the horizontal axis of a column or line chart, the vertical axis of a bar chart, the X axis of a scatter chart); 'value' is the other axis; 'secondary' is the secondary value axis of a combo chart.

value.description: Title of the value (Y) axis. On a combo chart, the primary (left) value axis.

secondary.description: Combo charts only: title of the secondary value axis at the right of the plot, drawn rotated like the primary value axis title. Dropped with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic on any other chart type and on a combo chart without 'secondaryAxis'.

ChartHighlight.description: Which series and categories a chart emphasizes. Names are matched exactly: series by data column name (after any 'fields' selection; a series is a plotted value column), categories by row label (the first column, or mapping.category), as text. A category label shared by several rows highlights each of them.

series.description: Series (value columns) to highlight: all marks of each named series. A name that is not a column is a 'chart-highlight-unknown-name' error; a column that is not plotted as a series (the category or X column, or one mapping.series leaves out) highlights nothing and is a 'chart-highlight-adapted' warning.

categories.description: Categories (row labels) to highlight: the marks of each named category (a column or bar of every series, a line's points, a pie or doughnut slice). A label no row has is a 'chart-highlight-unknown-name' error.

ChartDataLabels.description: Data label settings. A label shows the selected content parts in the fixed order category, value, percent, joined by the separator.

content.description: Which parts a label shows. Defaults to ['value']. 'percent' is the share of the total and exists only on pie and doughnut charts; 'category' shows the category name (the X value on a scatter chart). A part a chart type cannot show is dropped with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic.

position.description: Where a label sits relative to its mark. 'auto' (the default) is the type's default: outside-end for clustered columns and bars, pie slices and the histogram, pareto and waterfall constructs; center for stacked columns and bars; above for line and scatter points. Clustered columns and bars and the histogram, pareto and waterfall constructs take center, inside-end, inside-base and outside-end; stacked columns and bars take center, inside-end and inside-base; pie takes center, inside-end and outside-end; line and scatter points take above, below, left, right and center. Area, doughnut and radar charts and the funnel and treemap constructs take only 'auto' (the box-and-whisker and map constructs have no data labels). A combo chart places the labels of its column series like clustered columns and those of its line series like line points; a position only one part takes applies to that part, and the other part keeps its default (outside-end, above). An unsupported position falls back to 'auto' with a 'chart-option-adapted' diagnostic.

separator.description: Text between the parts of a label that shows more than one. Defaults to ', '.

Table.description: Table content, inline or dataset-backed. An inline table has 'rows' (required) and optional 'columns'. A dataset-backed table has 'dataset' (required) and optional 'fields', and no 'rows' or 'columns': it takes its headers, rows and column formats from the dataset (per-cell styles need an inline table).

columns.description: Optional column labels. Labels may be strings, rich runs, styled cell objects or DataColumn objects ({ "name", "format" }). A header's 'format' (DataColumn or StyledTableCell) is the column's number format; a body cell's own format wins. Null is an empty label or a placeholder covered by a preceding column span.

rows.description: Two-dimensional table row data; each row aligns by index with columns when columns are supplied.

dataset.description: Id of a top-level dataset that supplies this table's headers, rows and column formats. Excludes 'rows' and 'columns'. An unknown id is a 'dataset-unknown' error.

fields.description: Dataset tables only: the dataset columns to show, by name and in order. Absent shows every column. An unknown name is a 'dataset-field-unknown' error.

alt.description: Text alternative for the table: what it shows (the point and the key numbers), not 'a table'. The preview exposes it as the table's accessible name (role group with aria-label; the cells stay readable) and the PowerPoint export writes it as the table frame's alternative text (descr); import reads it back. An empty string hides a purely decorative table, with the same meaning as an empty Asset alt. The alt is a summary read before the cells, which stay readable, so it is most useful for a large or dense table; validate does not require one and does not report a missing one.
examples: North America grew 46% to $18.1M in Q4, ahead of EMEA at 40%.

ChartData.description: Inline tabular data driving a chart. The first column usually supplies category/x-axis labels; subsequent columns are plotted measures unless 'chart.mapping' or a chart type maps them differently. Value cells are numbers; a string is read only in strict decimal syntax ('12', '-3.5', '1e6'), and anything else ('12%', '$5', '(5)', '1,234') is a gap and a 'chart-value-not-numeric' warning.

columns.description: Ordered column labels for the chart data table. A label is a string or a DataColumn ({ "name", "format" }) whose number format the data labels, value axis and exported workbook use.

rows.description: Tabular chart rows. Each row aligns by index with columns.

source.description: Optional provenance: where this inline data came from. Engines never read, fetch or refresh it; they keep it through editing, export and re-import.

DataColumn.description: A named data column with an optional number format. Anywhere a chart or dataset column is a string it may be a DataColumn; the string form is { "name": value } with no format. A table column header may also be a DataColumn.

name.description: Column label, used as the series name, the table header and the name 'fields' and 'chart.mapping' address.

format.description: Number format of the column's number values (data labels, value axis, table cells, exported workbook). Absent: the General form.

DataSourceRef.description: Provenance of inline data or a dataset: the file, sheet and range it came from and when. Engines never read, fetch or refresh it; they keep it through editing, export and re-import. Re-import the data to update it.

src.description: Where the data came from: an 'asset:<id>' reference, a URL, or a relative or local path.

sheet.description: Sheet or table name inside a spreadsheet source.

range.description: A1-style range inside a spreadsheet source.

fields.description: The source fields the data was taken from, in order.

retrieved.description: When the data was taken from the source: an ISO 8601 date or date-time.

DatasetId.description: Id of an entry in the top-level datasets map (the assets id pattern).

DatasetFields.description: Dataset column names to use, in order, each at most once. Selects and orders the dataset's columns; an unknown name is a 'dataset-field-unknown' error.

Datasets.description: Shared data tables keyed by id (the assets id pattern). Charts reference one with 'chart.data': { "dataset": "<id>" } and tables with 'table': { "dataset": "<id>" }.

Dataset.description: One shared data table: named columns (strings or DataColumn objects with a number format) and rows of scalar cells. Column names are unique ('data-column-duplicate' error). Rich text and styling belong in an inline table.

title.description: Human name of the dataset, shown by editors.

rows.description: Rows of scalar cells (string, number, boolean, null); each row aligns by index with columns.

source.description: Optional provenance. Engines never read, fetch or refresh it.

DatasetRef.description: Chart data taken from a top-level dataset. Engines inline it before plotting; 'chart.mapping' names columns after the 'fields' selection.

dataset.description: Id of the dataset. An unknown id is a 'dataset-unknown' error.

fields.description: The dataset columns to use, by name and in order. Absent uses every column.

ChartMapping.description: Series mapping by column name (after any 'fields' selection). Mapping only selects and orders columns; pie, doughnut and other single-series constructs still plot one series. An unknown name is a 'chart-mapping-unknown-column' error; a series that repeats the category or X column, and an X column on a chart type without an X axis, are dropped with a 'chart-mapping-adapted' warning.

category.description: The label (category) column. Default: the first column.

x.description: The X column of an XY (scatter) chart. Default: the second column (the first, when the category is the second column), and only when there are three or more columns: with two, the second column is the one series, plotted against row numbers. An X that leaves no series is plotted as the series with a 'chart-mapping-adapted' warning.

series.description: The plotted columns, in order. Default: every column that is not the category or the X column.

ChartDataCell.description: A cell in inline chart data.

TableCell.description: A scalar, rich-run array, or styled/spanning cell object. Existing scalar and rich forms remain valid.

TableCellValue.description: A scalar table value or canonical rich text runs, without cell decoration or geometry.

value.description: Editable cell content; styling and spans do not change its scalar type or rich runs.

colSpan.description: Number of grid columns covered, starting at this cell. Covered positions must contain null. Default 1.

rowSpan.description: Number of grid rows covered, starting at this cell. Covered positions must contain null. Header cells cannot span into body rows. Default 1.

format.description: Number format. On a body cell it formats that cell's number value (and wins over the column's format); on a header cell (in 'columns') it is the column's format, the same as a DataColumn header. Strings, booleans, null and rich runs display unchanged.

StyledTableCell.description: A cell with explicit visual style or merged geometry. Its position remains its array column index; use null placeholders for every covered grid position.

fill.description: Cell background: a hex color, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference. Eight-digit hex colors include alpha; #00000000 is transparent.

color.description: Default text color, overridden by individual rich run colors. Accepts a hex color, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference.

align.description: Horizontal text alignment inside the cell.

verticalAlign.description: Vertical alignment inside the padded cell box.

borders.description: Independent cell edges. Omitted edges retain the table theme border; width 0 removes an edge.

TableCellStyle.description: Cell appearance. Sizes use reference pixels at a 720-pixel canvas short edge and scale with the slide.

TableCellPadding.description: Text insets in reference pixels. Defaults: top 8, right 10, bottom 4, left 10.

color.description: Border color: a hex color, a color-scheme slot or role name, or a 'var:<id>' variable reference. Eight-digit hex colors include alpha; #00000000 is transparent.

width.description: Border width in reference pixels; 0 removes this edge.

Catalogs.description:
The catalog records a document embeds, grouped by the catalog they came from. Each property is a group; inside a group, records are keyed by kind and then by id.
- 'default': the catalog bare ids come from. It needs a 'source' when it holds records. Omitted: bare ids fall back to the host's default catalog. false: no catalog fallback, so every bare id must be embedded (under 'custom' or 'default').
- 'custom': the records the document defines itself. It has no source.
- any other name ('acme'): an extra catalog, identified by its 'source'. The name is the prefix references use ('acme:hero'). Names are lowercase kebab-case; 'default' and 'custom' are reserved.

Resolution, for every kind: a bare id resolves in 'custom', then in the records embedded under 'default', then in the catalog the host registered for default.source (the host's default catalog when 'default' is omitted). 'name:id' resolves in that group's records, then in the catalog the host registered for its source. A reference written inside an embedded record (a theme's colorScheme) resolves in that record's own group first. A prefix that names no group is a validation error; a reference that resolves nowhere is the warning opf/unresolved-reference. Engines never fetch a source: hosts register catalogs by their source string, and authoring tools embed every record a document uses when they save it.

default.description: The catalog bare ids come from: its source and the records of it this document embeds. false turns off the catalog fallback for bare ids.

custom.description: Records the document defines itself, referenced by bare id. Checked first for every bare id. Forking a catalog record copies it here under a new id, so the change of ownership is visible.

propertyNames.description: Group name: lowercase kebab-case. 'default' and 'custom' are reserved.

additionalProperties.description: A named catalog: its source and the records of it this document embeds. References name it as a prefix ('acme:hero').

CatalogGroup.description: One catalog group: the catalog's source and the records of it the document embeds, by kind and then by id.

layouts.description: Layout records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-layout/v1. Referenced from Slide.layout.

themes.description: Theme records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-theme/v1. Referenced from design.theme.

colorSchemes.description: Colour-scheme records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-color-scheme/v1. Referenced from design.colorScheme and a theme's colorScheme.

fontSchemes.description: Font-scheme records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-font-scheme/v1. Referenced from design.fontScheme, a theme's fontScheme and a language's font schemes.

narratives.description: Narrative records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-narrative/v1. Referenced from narrative.

audiences.description: Audience records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-audience/v1. Referenced from audience.

purposes.description: Purpose records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-purpose/v1. Referenced from purpose.

tones.description: Tone records keyed by id, each with the fields of https://openpresentation.org/schema/opf-tone/v1. Referenced from tone.

CatalogSource.description: Identity of a catalog: an HTTPS URL ('https://www.pptx.gallery') or a package reference ('pkg:@acme/opf-catalog'). It names the catalog; engines never fetch or install it. A host registers the catalog's records under this exact string, and copying slides between documents matches groups by it.

CatalogRecords.description: Embedded records of one kind, keyed by id. The key is the record's id; an embedded record carries no '$schema', 'id', origin or digest. Catalog display metadata ('x-*' members) is stripped when a record is embedded.

additionalProperties.description: One embedded record: the fields of the kind's companion schema without '$schema' and 'id'.

CatalogReference.description: A content reference: a bare id ('two-column') or 'name:id' ('acme:hero'), where the prefix names a group of 'catalogs'. URLs and 'pkg:' strings are not references; a named catalog group replaces them. See Catalogs for the resolution order.

LanguageTag.description: A BCP-47 language tag ('en-US', 'ja', 'zh-Hans', 'sr-Latn-ME'), an engine vocabulary. Use 'en-GB' for UK English; 'en-UK' is not a valid region.

Composition.description: Portable dynamic composition. Slide fields override the resolved layout. Nested groups (content groups here, placeholder groups in a layout record) arrange their children independently, inheriting only minFontSize and overflow. Explicit promoted regions retain their positions.

mode.description: auto chooses a grid from available space and content; grid uses columns; row and column use one horizontal or vertical track.

columns.description: Column count for grid. In auto mode this caps the number of columns.

gap.description: Space between cells as a fraction of the container short edge (canvas at slide root). Default 0.03333333333333333.

padding.description: Inset as a fraction of the container short edge. Default 0.08 on a slide, 0 inside a group.

weights.description: Relative track sizes: columns for row/grid/auto, rows for column. Omitted tracks have weight 1; extra weights are ignored.

minFontSize.description: Minimum readable text size in reference pixels at a 720-pixel canvas short edge. Default 16. Overflow is diagnosed when text cannot fit at this size.

overflow.description: warn returns diagnostics for content that does not fit; error rejects layout. Content is never silently removed. Default warn.
